# Charter review: docs-draft

Scope: `technical-design/markdown-units.md` (new note, full review) and the six other files `CHANGES.md`
lists as touched, diffed against their current `docs/` versions. Compared against
`docs/README.md` (the charter), `docs/_templates/note.md`, and both folder `README.md` indexes.

## Form findings

Departures from the charter's or the template's mechanical rules — frontmatter, headings, callout
kind, Related line, file naming — independent of whether the prose itself is accurate.

### 1. A subheading in the new note carries no emoji

`technical-design/markdown-units.md:36` | rule: docs/README.md:65, "Every heading in a note opens with
one emoji chosen for its subject (`## 💽 Modeling`, `### 🔑 Login`)" — the template's own house style
gives an `### 🔑 Login` example specifically to show the rule reaches `h3`, not only `h2`. | quoted span:
`### A list split around a nested code block` | departs: no emoji, unlike every other heading in this
note and every `h3` elsewhere in the touched files (`### ⬇️ Acquisition…`, `### 💬 An image's spoken
form…` in `article-extraction.md`).

### 2. The new note is linked inline from `item-contract.md` but not listed in its Related line

`technical-design/item-contract.md:30` (draft) adds `(see [markdown-units](markdown-units.md))` inline,
the only inline reference to the new note in this file. `technical-design/item-contract.md:99` (draft,
unchanged from current) | rule: docs/README.md:69, "Close a note with a `---` rule and a `Related:` line
linking the notes it actually touches." | quoted span: `Related: [item-lifecycle](item-lifecycle.md) ·
[article-extraction](article-extraction.md) · [read-along-timing](read-along-timing.md) ·
[authentication](authentication.md) · [persistence-and-storage](persistence-and-storage.md) ·
[queue](../product-design/queue.md)` | departs: `markdown-units` is missing from this line even though
the note now touches it. Every other file `CHANGES.md` lists as changed (`recipes.md`,
`extraction-service.md`, `article-extraction.md`) added `markdown-units` to its Related line; this one
did not, and `CHANGES.md`'s own entry for `item-contract.md` doesn't mention the Related line at all,
so the omission wasn't a deliberate choice recorded anywhere.

## Findings that turn on content, not just form

### 3. The new note's WARNING doesn't name how the failure presents or whether anything catches it, and cites no real occurrence

`technical-design/markdown-units.md:91-92` | rule: docs/README.md:51, "`> [!WARNING]`: a failure mode:
what breaks, how it presents, and whether anything catches it. Prefer failures that have actually
happened." | quoted span: "Inventory and leftover-text checks confirm that every element in the
container is accounted for and that no readable text was dropped. Neither confirms that a unit's
markdown syntax, such as a heading's `#`, a quote's `>` or a list's numbering, survived the
conversion." | departs: the callout says what the validator fails to check, but never says how the
failure presents to a listener (what they'd actually hear — presumably a heading read as plain prose
with no rise in it, or similar) or whether anything downstream catches it. It also names no concrete
instance, unlike the sibling callouts in the same batch of files that do: the sockpuppet.org `❦`
example in `article-extraction.md`'s WARNING, the New Yorker contact-sheet example in its image-validation
NOTE, and the Railway `libcairo2` gap in its SVG WARNING. This one reads as a theoretical gap rather
than an observed failure.

### 4. The new note's worked example runs well past the snippet-length rule

`technical-design/markdown-units.md:38-51` (the HTML input) and `:56-66` (the three markdown/plain-text
outputs) | rule: docs/README.md:63, "Explain the code, do not reprint it… a snippet appears only where
the code itself is the insight… Two to four lines when it happens." | quoted span: the fenced HTML
block runs 14 lines; the three output blocks that follow run 6, 1, and 3 lines. | departs, arguably: the
rule as written targets reprinting *implementation* code, and this is a synthetic worked example
illustrating the split/resume mechanism rather than a copy of a declaration, so it may fall outside the
rule's intent. Flagged because it's the one passage in this batch that clearly exceeds the stated
line count, and the charter gives no separate allowance for worked examples the way the template gives
one for a table's example row ("with an example only where the shape is not obvious from the
description").

## What did not turn up a finding

- Frontmatter on `markdown-units.md` (title, summary as a sentence about the subject, `created`) matches
  the template exactly.
- Every other heading in every touched file carries exactly one emoji.
- Callout kinds are used correctly throughout: each `NOTE` states a real choice and why, each `WARNING`
  elsewhere in the batch names a concrete failure, each `TIP` names a rejected alternative and the
  constraint it failed.
- No decision-record content (no requirements table, acceptance criteria, user story, or status ladder)
  in any draft.
- No `used to` / `previously` / `no longer` / narrative-history language; present tense throughout.
- No hard wrapping: every paragraph in every file is one line.
- Mermaid used for every shape (the new note's flowchart included; `CHANGES.md` records it was already
  run through the mermaid validator).
- No links to issues, and no mention of Linear, tasks, or ownership in any draft (the one Linear mention
  in `technical-design/README.md` is pre-existing, unchanged content, not something the draft added).
- `markdown-units.md` is linked from four existing notes (`recipes.md`, `extraction-service.md`,
  `article-extraction.md`, `item-contract.md`) and has a row in `technical-design/README.md`'s index, in
  the position `CHANGES.md` describes (between `recipes` and `extraction-service`).
- Closing `---` + `Related:` line present in every file, save the omission in finding 2.
- `markdown-units.md` is a unique file name across `docs/` (checked, no collision).
- No contradiction found between any two drafts, or between a draft and an unchanged note. In
  particular: the title-echo rule (recipes.md's authoring-prompt sentence, markdown-units.md's table row
  and NOTE, and what-gets-read-aloud.md's rewritten opening) agrees across all three; the spoken-form
  rules for list items, task checkboxes, tables, and comparison operators agree word-for-sense across
  `article-extraction.md` and `what-gets-read-aloud.md`; the sanitize-tail description agrees across
  `article-extraction.md` and `the-describer.md`.
